sections.content: How many people stayed in Chorley after gaining qualifications?

Chorley is a medium-sized town in the North West. Chorley does not have its own university.

Chorley has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Chorley ended up with:

  • a similar number of graduates as it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,710 state-school pupils from Chorley who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 505 (30%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 530 (31%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Chorley to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Chorley's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Chorley in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Chorley move to?

Of Chorley's graduates, 195 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 65 of those graduates (33%) were living fairly locally, in the Preston travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Chorley's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 145 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 70 of those qualified non-graduates (48%) were living fairly locally, in the Preston travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Chorley's GCSE cohort:

  • 80 graduates left the North West
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 30 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North West

In 2018 to 2019, 34% of graduates and 36% of qualified non-graduates living in Chorley had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 465 graduates and 585 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Chorley. This is compared with the 505 graduates and 530 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 66% of the graduates had also lived in Chorley as GCSE pupils, while 34% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Chorley in 2018 to 2019, 64% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 36% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
